pathways.climate_pressure: Drought losses described in Afgoye programme communities at2026endline.
pathways.documented_impact: Residents described agricultural losses and disrupted livelihoods.
pathways.fcv_mediator: Recurring armed conflict blocked access to farms and roads to markets in Jambaluul and Buula Madino.
pathways.possible_consequence: Insecurity compounds drought losses and restricts households' ability to sustain food and income access.
alternative_explanations: Input and food prices, aid changes, market demand and other livelihood constraints may also influence losses.
pathways.uncertainty: Named-community qualitative account in a non-counterfactual programme evaluation; no separate climate/conflict effect size or national extrapolation.
resilience_factors: Water-supported gardening examples elsewhere in the programme are not assumed effective in these two conflict-affected communities.
pathways.compact_statement: In Jambaluul/Buula Madino, conflict blocked farms and market routes and compounded drought-related livelihood losses.

gaps: The local Afgoye case is not assigned the report's broader30%market-access statistic.
Cooperative meeting barriers apply to526members, not all3,889surveyed households.
The expired2025year-end displacement projection was excluded from operational evidence.

executive_assessment.text: Jambaluul/Buula Madino provide named examples of conflict restricting farms and markets during drought, while cooperative attendance data show a programme-participation constraint.

Water access conditions uptake in named El Barde communities. Resource committees and women's land access provide reported peace/institutional capacities, with short-duration and non-counterfactual limitations.
